title: Grokking the System Design Interview
description: The classic course: a step-by-step interview framework, 16 worked designs from TinyURL to Ticketmaster, and the building blocks every design uses.

chapters.title: System Design Interviews: A step by step guide
Designing a URL Shortening service like TinyURL
chapters.lead: Let's design a URL shortening service like TinyURL. This service will provide short aliases redirecting to long URLs.

chapters.title: Designing Pastebin
chapters.lead: Let's design a Pastebin like web service, where users can store plain text. Users of the service will enter a piece of text and get a randomly generated URL to access it.

chapters.title: Designing Instagram
chapters.lead: Let's design a photo-sharing service like Instagram, where users can upload photos to share them with other users.

chapters.title: Designing Dropbox
chapters.lead: Let's design a file hosting service like Dropbox or Google Drive. Cloud file storage enables users to store their data on remote servers. Usually, these servers are maintained by cloud storage providers and made available to users over a network (typically through the Internet). Users pay for their cloud data storage on a monthly basis.

chapters.title: Designing Facebook Messenger
chapters.lead: Let's design an instant messaging service like Facebook Messenger where users can send text messages to each other through web and mobile interfaces.

chapters.title: Designing Twitter
chapters.lead: Let's design a Twitter-like social networking service. Users of the service will be able to post tweets, follow other people, and favorite tweets.

chapters.title: Designing Youtube or Netflix
chapters.lead: Let's design a video sharing service like Youtube, where users will be able to upload/view/search videos.

chapters.title: Designing Typeahead Suggestion
chapters.lead: Let's design a real-time suggestion service, which will recommend terms to users as they enter text for searching.

chapters.title: Designing an API Rate Limiter
chapters.lead: Let's design an API Rate Limiter which will throttle users based upon the number of the requests they are sending.

chapters.title: Designing Twitter Search
chapters.lead: Twitter is one of the largest social networking service where users can share photos, news, and text-based messages. In this chapter, we will design a service that can store and search user tweets. Similar Problems: Tweet search.

chapters.title: Designing a Web Crawler
chapters.lead: Let's design a Web Crawler that will systematically browse and download the World Wide Web. Web crawlers are also known as web spiders, robots, worms, walkers, and bots.

chapters.title: Designing Facebook’s Newsfeed
chapters.similar: Twitter Newsfeed, Instagram Newsfeed, Quora Newsfeed
chapters.lead: Let's design Facebook's Newsfeed, which would contain posts, photos, videos, and status updates from all the people and pages a user follows.

chapters.title: Designing Yelp or Nearby Friends
chapters.lead: Let's design a Yelp like service, where users can search for nearby places like restaurants, theaters, or shopping malls, etc., and can also add/view reviews of places.

chapters.title: Designing Uber backend
chapters.similar: Lyft, Didi, Via, Sidecar etc. Difficulty level: Hard Prerequisite: Designing Yelp
chapters.lead: Let's design a ride-sharing service like Uber, which connects passengers who need a ride with drivers who have a car.

chapters.title: Design Ticketmaster
chapters.lead: Let's design an online ticketing system that sells movie tickets like Ticketmaster or BookMyShow.

chapters.title: Long-Polling vs WebSockets vs Server-Sent Events
chapters.lead: What is the difference between Long-Polling, WebSockets, and Server-Sent Events?
